Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’m starting with the workspace contract and the mandated fish-control bookshelf. I’ll then inspect the inherited rollout evidence—including both moving-window visual views—before proposing or editing the single candidate.

The skills constrain this to normalized body-frame feedback and require visual/metric agreement. I’m now anchoring the comparison to the assigned parent guidance and inspecting the available rollout artifacts before opening the bookshelf references or drafting the hypothesis.

All four rollouts satisfy the direct-uniform still-water contract. The strongest candidate reaches 2.46 L but later exits the left boundary; the prefilled velocity-lead variant reaches only 7.33 L and eventually exits low after reversing progress. I’m inspecting those two combined sheets now to distinguish useful steering from merely dramatic wake structure.

The visual comparison shows the key split: the response-gated redirect preserves a coherent staggered wake and produces substantial approach, but it sails past the target and continues out the left side; the velocity-lead variant over-curves into a broad loop and loses closure, while shared mean curvature immediately turns away and exits upward. Per the bookshelf protocol, I’m consulting mechanism invariants now; any adopted idea will be translated only through body-frame target and measured turn response.

The trajectory cross-check sharpens the target: the best redirect has ample propulsion but delays downward correction, passing the target on its upper-left side at 2.46 L around 24.23 T; the prefill’s stronger velocity-lead/tail-curvature combination corrects downward too aggressively, loops, and departs with negative progress. I’m reading the inherited worker notes and exact controller variants next so the candidate changes a mechanism with a falsifiable middle ground, not an unsupported gain sweep.

I’ll use one compact mechanism: keep the best response-gated C-bend, but during the final approach require both correct-sign yaw and velocity alignment with the body-frame target vector before releasing the redirect. This preserves the far-field gait and only holds extra curvature when the fish is physically sliding past the capture corridor. The fish-control shelf directly shaped this approach-hold gate; I’m recording its transfer and falsification criteria before touching the policy, as required.

The inherited notes’ saturation warning also survives direct checking: roughly 96–98% of raw-action rows in the seed, best redirect, and velocity-lead runs exceed the acceleration envelope before evaluator clipping. I’m therefore keeping the successful redirect amplitude fixed and changing only its state-based release condition. The durable guidance update will capture both the comparative rollout lesson and this applicability boundary.

The candidate, notes, and durable lesson are all updated. I’m now invoking the mandated check-runner defined by `.codex/agents/check-runner.toml`; it will validate guidance provenance, the finite two-joint Julia contract (including parameter ownership), and the editable-file boundary without running CFD.

The configured check-runner could not start because its fixed `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unavailable on this account. I’m following the runner’s exact three-command contract manually instead, still without CFD; if any check fails, I’ll repair and rerun it.

The first check found a rendered-workspace metadata defect: `README.md` contains the identical “copied to guidance” parent marker twice, so provenance cannot identify exactly one assigned parent. This is the same defect recorded in inherited worker logs. I’m removing only the duplicate marker, then rerunning the check.

All three mandated checks now pass after the duplicate parent marker repair. I’m adding one final non-CFD behavioral check: the new policy must be exactly identical to the sampled winner outside 4.5 L and during aligned near-target motion, while holding more same-sign redirect only for the recorded near-miss geometry.

Produced exactly one candidate: [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:11).

- Adds capture-aligned redirect release while preserving the strongest sampled carrier.
- Recorded visual diagnosis, bookshelf transfer, and falsification in [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1).
- Added the comparative reusable lesson in [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:35).
- Removed the duplicated parent marker from [README.md](README.md:123).

All three required non-CFD checks pass, including parameter ownership and solver boundary. A behavioral check confirms unchanged far/aligned behavior and stronger same-sign redirect for the recorded near miss. The configured check-runner agent itself was unavailable due to its fixed model, so its exact commands were executed manually. No CFD was run.
